item.title: Book Club for November 2026 — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Gayle Graham It is a pleasure to invite you to the November 5th Icelandic Roots Book Club to hear from Cathie Eliasson, the author of Falcons Forever: the Saga of the 1920 Olympic Gold Medal Ice Hockey Team. The book chronicles the Winnipeg Falcons' journey to the VII Olympiad in Antwerp, Belgium, where they won the very first gold medal in men's ice hockey. item.title: Rok — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Gunnar Birgisson The weather plays an oversized role in Icelandic life, much more so than in most other places. And when it comes to weather, the wind is a major player. In Iceland, the wind is such a constant element of life that people can be surprised when there’s a day without notable wind. The complete absence of wind, logn, can leave people baffled, as if their long-time nemesis had unexpectedly retreated, probably to prepare for a more vicious attack. Rok is just one type of...

item.title: Kotnúpur - Bjarni — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Bryndís Viglundsdóttir The Icelandic Writers Group contributes to the bi-weekly Rætur Fréttir/Roots News with stories relating to our current theme of the year. For 2026, we are profiling our Icelandic ancestors settling in North America. Bryndís brings us a personal story of yearning for that new world that was vicariously fulfilled many years later. The West Fjords of Iceland are a region of deep fjords, high mountains, and blue skies. The blue skies change quickly and become grey and...

item.description: On August 1, 2026, Icelandic Roots broke ground on Rootshús. Since then, construction has moved quickly, and the building is taking shape. item.title: Saskatchewan Icelandic History Driving Tour — Icelandic Roots
item.description: by Karen Pytlowany and Shaune Jonasson Icelandic settlements in North America progressed west over the years with many settlers filing homestead grants in Saskatchewan. Fewer came directly from Iceland, whereas numerous settlers arrived from the Argyle district in Manitoba, North Dakota and Minnesota.
